title: Bill Robinson tour, Estelle Edson and Marl Young
summary: Love goes through a programme of the Bo Jangles tour and Fields remembers singer Estelle Edson and her friendship with Marl Young.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, you were young as a son of a gun, you're a little older now. Here's one where you're on tour with Bill Robinson, Bo Jangles. Ernie Fields' orchestra, Ross McLean, Jimmy Smith--was he the one who danced on the vibes?
I saw him in Atlantic City. Estelle Edson--you know--and Mel Moore--I used to see Estelle around Los Angeles a lot with Marl Young, they were good friends.

They were. I think they were engaged and I think Estelle told him-- of course, to each his own--but she just went overhead religiously so until--I don't know some kind of thought she was out of her mind, she was over everything, and of course, Marl was to the extreme the other way, some of them considered him an infidel.
Yeah. So they just didn't get along, but they were very, very tight.
I used to see them together.
I remember one trip I made, she left the band and she headed out to Denver--you know, she was teaching in L.A.
Yeah she was teaching and it got so far that I think she had a little radio show or something in there and I was in town and she invited me to dinner and had Marl out.
